decisions.text: ticket-v2 is compiled from a census over the rehearsal records' decision lines, never authored first. The census is a COUNT, not an extraction (there is no 'noun a line settles' to identify). Its algorithm, run 2026-09-16 over 16 records (the ten required are met): for every record under CairnCommons/rehearsals/ open the ticket it names and read decisions[]; count (a) each key a decision line carries and how many lines carry it — measured n 70, text 70, by 70, step 37, source 37, amended 5, folded_text 4; (b) each line's by-kind from its leading words — measured 'Akien verbatim' 22, 'CC at cast' 4, 'CC under rehearsal' 20, 'derived from' 3, unlabeled 21; (c) each gap's step, a D-line id or a prose step — measured 69 D-lines, 72 prose; (d) per ticket, which prose fields are present — intention, why, how, traces_to, cast_checks, challenge_at_birth on all four. Schema rule from the counts: a key on every line is required (n, text, by); a key on every line added under rehearsal is required for such lines (step, source); a key that appears only on revision is optional (amended, folded_text); the prose fields the gaps name as steps are dropped (D6's list). WHERE THE CENSUS DATA IS: before this build it is the measurement file /tmp/claude-1000/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/a187d6ab-5944-4bda-9405-365b2b200f92/scratchpad/census_v2.json (absolute path; measured 2026-09-16 21:59 to exist, 1 file, sha256 4b8e394bfe8d9602ceb17e8f3859735f6af414c8e92a879ed1b0ddd5e1d3ae79; the build's FIRST act is to read it — if it is absent or its sha differs the build is RED and stops, and nothing re-measures: a re-measurement is a new census on a new day and needs a new decision line, never an improvised step; a JSON object with keys measured, by, records, gap_kinds, gap_step_shape, decision_line_keys, by_kinds, tickets, per_record, reading); the build copies that object verbatim into CairnCommons/tickets/_schema-v2.json under the key census, and that file is committed to the CairnCommons git repo, so every later builder reads the census from git and never from a scratchpad. A rerun on a later day is a python3 script implementing steps (a)-(d) over CairnCommons/rehearsals/*.json and the tickets they name — no LLM — and the schema file's census.how carries that one-paragraph algorithm so the rerun needs nothing else.

decisions.text: Every decision line carries a `by` in one of four shapes — 'Akien verbatim <date>', 'derived from <address>', 'CC at cast <date>', 'CC under rehearsal <record>' — and the door refuses a line without one. IMPLEMENTATION: a judge inside judge_packet in skills/sorted/door.py, riding the one refusal every other lack rides: for each element of the packet's decisions list, append a lack {field: 'decisions', why: 'line <n>: <what is wrong>'} unless the element is a dict carrying n (int), text (non-empty str) and by (str) whose by starts with one of the four prefixes 'Akien verbatim ', 'derived from ', 'CC at cast ', 'CC under rehearsal ' (prefix match, case-sensitive); every offending line is named, not only the first; an empty or absent decisions list is the flat contract's lack (the seam reads every contract field as required and non-empty) and is not reported twice. Lines the rehearsal machine adds later with --decide carry by 'CC' plus step and source 'rehearsal'; they are post-cast lines the door never sees, and the schema names that pair as the 'CC under rehearsal <record>' shape's realisation — no edit to the rehearsal machine.

BUILD ORDER inside this one voyage: first the charter skills/sorted/intention+why.json gains the two contract fields decisions and intent_berth (that is D15's act, done before any line of door.py is edited); then file_ticket is written. The check that the two fields are present and non-empty is NOT new code: the standing seam cairn/machines/learning_block/learning_block.py:219 inspect_input already refuses any contract field that is absent or empty, so adding the fields to the charter IS the check — the only new judge in door.py is the by check on each line (D4). THE INPUT is the sorted packet, which after that charter change ALWAYS carries decisions (a list of lines) and intent_berth (the absolute path of the /intent berth) — both required, non-empty, refused by name when absent. THE FUNCTION is file_ticket(payload, berth, *, commons) in door.py, called from fire() after sb.fire returns and only when payload['exit'] == 'routed_forward' (a routed_out packet berths and files nothing): it reads from_idea and task_or_ticket out of the intent berth's answers; mints the id as secrets.token_hex(6), redrawn while a file <hex>-* already stands in the tickets store; builds the v2 ticket from the packet's own fields — id, title, node_class, task_or_ticket, workflow_and_state (the packet's workflow), date and created (today), author ('CC via /sorted'), from_idea, intent_berth, sorted_berth (= result['berth'], the path sb.fire returned), owner (the packet's gates_bound owner if named, else 'CC'), owning_intention (the packet's owning_intention if present, else the title), questions (the packet's questions), falsifier (the packet's falsifier_check), watchme, depends_on ([]), follow_ons (the packet's children unless it is a 'none, because' string, then []), schema_version 'ticket-v2', rehearsal 'none-yet', decisions (the packet's list verbatim); writes <hex>-<title>.json under <commons>/tickets/ through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(path, json text, verb='cast', why='/sorted cast <hex> <title>: sorted berth <berth>') — 'cast' is the verb every ticket write already journals under; commons is the injected kwarg fire() already accepts (the proof's scratch commons) or, when None, the live commons the door's other judges default to (_COMMONS). THE OUTPUT: the dict fire() returns gains ticket_path (absolute) and ticket_id (the hex), and main() prints it as it prints the berth today.

decisions.text: The schema file CairnCommons/tickets/_schema-v2.json is one JSON object with exactly three top-level keys: schema_version (the string 'ticket-v2'), schema, and census (the D3 measurement copied in verbatim, plus census.how, the one-paragraph rerun algorithm). schema is an object mapping each kept field to its one-line meaning, spelled here so nothing is inferred: id — the 12-hex ticket identifier minted at cast; title — the slug the file is named by (<id>-<title>.json); node_class — the class in CairnCommons/node_classes/ (e.g. code-seam); task_or_ticket — 'ticket' or 'task' as /intent answered it; workflow_and_state — the rendered workflow string with its cursor in brackets; date and created — the cast date, ISO yyyy-mm-dd; author — who cast it (e.g. 'CC (Opus 5), session <id>'); from_idea — the id under CairnCommons/ideas/ or 'none, because <X>'; intent_berth — absolute path of the /intent berth; sorted_berth — absolute path of the /sorted berth; owner — who gates writes to the component (a charter address or a name); owning_intention — the charter or homeless-intention address the ticket serves; questions — list of open-<id> question ids or 'none, because <X>'; falsifier — the one prose field kept, the done/wrong-intent test; watchme — the WATCHME spec object or 'none, because <X>'; depends_on — list of ticket ids or texts this ticket waits on; follow_ons — list of child ticket ids or first-cut names; schema_version — 'ticket-v2'; rehearsal — the latest rehearsal record path or 'none-yet'; decisions — a list of {n (int, 1-based), text (one line), by (provenance, one of the four shapes) required; step and source required on a line added under rehearsal; amended and folded_text optional}. Nothing in the file is authored beyond these one-line meanings; the field set is D6's list as the census confirmed it.

decision_verbatim:
1. so we're getting buried in 'things akien has to look at' again, and i can't keep up. My day job isn't doing well because even with the reduced time i spend here, it's still not enough focus on the day job. and since we have no funding other than my day job, continuing to fall behind is a problem. but had a conversation with haiku that i have been egar to share with you, and i think it could reframe everything in front of us:
if i say 'i want tickets so well written that haiku can reliably build them' is not going to be as effective as 'reading the ticket as haiku, point out every unanswered question so we can take another pass at getting them answered before the build' is it? how can i do it even better?

Haiku sez:
You're right—the second approach is dramatically more effective because it's observable. You see exactly where the model hesitated, guessed, or filled in gaps with its own assumptions.

But you can go further. Instead of just pointing out unanswered questions, try this:

Have Haiku show its proof skeleton.

Don't ask it to critique. Ask it to build a sketch of what it would construct with the ticket as-is, step by step. Show you:

Every assumption it's making
Every branch point where it could go two ways
Where it felt confident vs. where it guessed
What it would need to see change for each guess to become certainty
Then you look at that skeleton and either recognize it ("yes, that's exactly what I meant") or catch the divergence ("no, I meant path B, not A").

Or even better: comparative reading.

Feed the ticket to Haiku three times (or to Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus) without the outputs seeing each other. Compare their proof skeletons. Every place they diverge is a gap, and the kind of divergence tells you what matters:

Same structure, different details? → Implementation clarity
Different structures? → Fundamental underspecification

Or interactive narrowing:
